messages:
ria: quick check — ran an "early-rollforward" decode variant on raven-7b-quant. wanted to share numbers and get quick ops/qa advice. pinging @sam and @alex :eyes:

ria: short summary: p50/p95 token latency improves a lot; end-to-end LLM request p95 down ~27-30% on short-medium prompts. quality: small regressions on sensitive QA and some instruction-following prompts (~0.4–0.8% absolute on EE/EM depending on metric).

sam: can you paste the exact eval harness and dataset? also which quant config?

ria: sure — eval harness: 2k mixed prompts (500 instruction, 700 openQA, 500 completion, 300 context-heavy). metrics: EM for QA, BLEU-ish for short completions, and mean gpt-eval score (multi-seed). quant: int8 symmetric with per-tensor scale, channel-wise for attention weights.

ria: results (baseline = raven-7b-quant w/ greedy decode)
```
config: early_rollforward=true, threshold=0.62, patience=2, fallback=baseline
hardware: A100-40GB, batch=8, seq=512
metrics:
  p50_tok: baseline=8.2ms -> rollforward=6.1ms
  p95_tok: baseline=25.1ms -> rollforward=17.8ms
  request_p95: baseline=410ms -> rollforward=295ms
  QA_EM: baseline=72.4 -> rollforward=71.8
  GPT_mean: baseline=3.84 -> rollforward=3.78
  rerun_rate (fallback): ~3.2% (auto re-eval triggered when score variance high)
```

ria: notes: most wins are for short queries where the predictor avoids full-token softmax; for long-context (>1024) the benefit shrinks to ~10% p95. fallback triggers on logprob anomalies and on high topk entropy.

bench-bot: automated: full-run artifacts uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-experiments/early-rollforward/4307654321/ (profiles, token traces, diffs).

alex: interesting. did you try this with kv-cache reuse enabled across request sequences (conversational workloads)? curious if prediction harms cache-hit alignment and increases divergence later in conversation.

ria: yes — did a small convo sim: session reuse enabled; divergence measured by token-level KL over next-20 tokens. divergence is negligible (<0.02 avg KL) for >95% sessions. worst-case outliers correlated with very long system prompts where the predictor misfires early. fallback prevented end-user visible regression in our sim.

maya: can you paste 2–3 concrete failure examples (prompt + baseline output vs rollforward output)? will spin up a small human eval on those if it's clear.

ria: pasted below (shortened):
---
prompt: "Summarize the legal obligations for remote contractors in CA."
baseline: "In California, employers must... (mentions worker classification, taxable withholding)"
rollforward: "Employers should ensure tax withholding..."  // misses explicit worker classification clause -> small factual drop
---
prompt: "Write a polite refusal to a feature request that compromises data privacy."
baseline: "Thanks for the idea... we can't implement due to privacy and legal constraints."
rollforward: "Thanks for the idea. Unfortunately, this conflicts with our policies." // softer, less specific
---
ria: these are the sorts of drift cases — mostly loss of a short explicit clause.

sam: thanks. i think a cautious canary rollout is reasonable. suggest canary config: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% over 24h with automatic rollback on quality_regression > 0.5 EM points on sample probes and latency SLA miss. also enable tracing for rerun events.

ops-bot: noting deployment risk: early-rollforward uses a new predictor microservice. add health-check endpoint + circuit-breaker. require canary flag and 12h log retention for quick rollback analysis.

alex: one more ask — do we have a cheap distillation of the predictor model (quantized small MLP) so warmup cost is tiny? if not, consider swapping to a 1M-10M param predictor to reduce overhead.

ria: current predictor is ~3.2M params (quant int8). warmup cost ~4ms per GPU, amortized across bursts. good to test smaller variant — i'll queue a run.

maya: i'll take the three failure examples into the human eval batch (n=200 each, compare baseline vs rollforward). will report back tomorrow with rater-level diffs.

ria: next steps: 1) canary rollout plan per sam; 2) smaller predictor experiment (alex); 3) human eval from maya; 4) keep fallback aggressive for first 48h.

ria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
